chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa and Muhammad ibn Abi Abdillah and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, all together from al-Hasan ibn al-Abbas ibn al-Harish, from Abu Ja'far al-Thani عليه السلام, that Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام said:
To Ibn Abbas: Indeed, Laylat al-Qadr is in every year, and in that night the command of the year descends, and for that command there are authorities after Rasul Allah صلى الله عليه وآله.
So Ibn Abbas said, 'Who are they?' He said, 'I and eleven from my loins, Imams who are muhaddathun.'

key_terms.أَمْرُ السَّنَةِ: the decree or command pertaining to the coming year
key_terms.رَسُولِ اللَّهِ: the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله
key_terms.لَيْلَةَ الْقَدْرِ: Laylat al-Qadr, the Night of Ordainment occurring each year
key_terms.مُحَدَّثُونَ: those spoken to or addressed, i.e. recipients of divine communication short of prophethood
key_terms.وُلَاةٌ: authorities or guardians entrusted with the command

ai.seo_question: Who are the authorities of the divine command after Rasul Allah صلى الله عليه وآله according to this hadith on Laylat al-Qadr?
ai.summary: This hadith states that Laylat al-Qadr occurs every year and that the yearly divine command descends in it. It further identifies enduring divinely appointed authorities after Rasul Allah صلى الله عليه وآله as Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام and eleven Imams from his progeny, described as muhaddathun.
